newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina joins tobacco lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina joins tobacco lawsuit.

text.p: South Carolina has added its name to the list of states suing the tobacco industry to recover money spent treating smoking-related illnesses, the state attorney general's office said Tuesday.

Attorney General Charlie Condon said he decided to file the lawsuit, which was filed Monday in the Richland County Court of Common Pleas, after the recent admissions of Liggett Group Inc. Chief Executive Bennett LeBow that the tobacco industry did target minors, knew its products caused disease and knew tobacco was addictive.
"But I also think our tobacco farmers deserve representation in this litigation, since they have not deliberately set out to encourage young people to smoke," Condon said in a statement.

The state, one of 29 states and municipalities to have sued the tobacco industry, also plans to join settlement talks with cigarette makers. Mississippi became the first state to try to recoup Medicaid costs of smokers when it filed suit against the industry in May 1994.

Missouri said Monday that it also had filed suit. Defendants named in Missouri's lawsuit included: Philip Morris Cos. Inc.; R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.; American Tobacco Inc.; Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc; B.A.T Industries Plc; British American Tobacco Co. Ltd.; Liggett & Myers Inc., a unit of Brooke Group; Lorillard Tobacco Co., a unit of Loews Corp.; United States Tobacco Co., a unit of UST Inc.

The suit also named the public relations firm of Hill & Knowlton Inc. and industry lobby groups such as the Council for Tobacco Research USA Inc., Smokeless Tobacco Council Inc. and the Tobacco Institute.
